parts.zh: M: 最初的店是由一位名叫 Gruby 的退休印刷工开办的
W: 那么，他后来是如何着手创办这项业务的呢？
M: 他先寻找市场上已经有的适合左撇子使用的产品
W: 明白了。所以，你们有一部分库存是委托定制的
M: 嗯，距离 Gruby 先生最初尝试已经过去了二十五到三十年
W: 你们的库存品种有哪些？
M: 品种包括各种剪刀
W: 竞争情况怎么样？你们的竞争对手多吗？

items.stem: What kind of business is the man engaged in?

choices.text: Providing aid to the disabled.
choices.zh: 为残障人士提供援助。

choices.text: Selling products made for left-handers.
choices.zh: 销售为左撇子制造的产品。

choices.text: Promoting products for manufacturers.
choices.zh: 为制造商推广产品。

choices.text: Printing labels for manufactured goods.
choices.zh: 为制成品印刷标签。

items.stem: What does the man say about his stock of products?

choices.text: About half of them are unavailable on the market.
choices.zh: 其中约一半在市场上买不到。

choices.text: The kitchenware in his shop is of unique design.
choices.zh: 他店里的厨具设计独特。

choices.text: All of them are manufactured in his own plant.
choices.zh: 所有产品都在他自己的工厂生产。

choices.text: Most of them are specially made for his shop.
choices.zh: 其中大部分是专门为他的店铺定制的。

items.stem: What can we know about the business of left-handed products?

choices.text: It is the man who is talking that set up the business.
choices.zh: 是正在说话的这位男士创立了这项业务。

choices.text: There was more competition in the business about 30 years ago.
choices.zh: 大约30年前这个行业的竞争更激烈。

choices.text: There are more left-handed products on the market now.
choices.zh: 现在市场上有更多左撇子产品。

choices.text: People in the business should run stores to sell products.
choices.zh: 从事该行业的人应该开设店铺销售产品。

items.stem: What does the man say about other people in his line of business?

choices.text: They specialise in one product only.
choices.zh: 他们只专营一种产品。

choices.text: They have outlets throughout Britain.
choices.zh: 他们在全英国都有销售网点。

choices.text: They run chain stores in central London.
choices.zh: 他们在伦敦市中心经营连锁店。

choices.text: They sell by mail order only.
choices.zh: 他们只通过邮购方式销售。

items.stem: What do we learn about the man's company?

choices.text: It publishes magazines.
choices.zh: 它出版杂志。

choices.text: It is engaged in product design.
choices.zh: 它从事产品设计。

choices.text: It sponsors trade fairs.
choices.zh: 它赞助商品交易会。

choices.text: It runs sales promotion campaigns.
choices.zh: 它开展促销活动。

items.stem: Why was the campaign delayed according to the man?

choices.text: The woman's company failed to make payments in time.
choices.zh: 这位女士的公司未能按时付款。

choices.text: The ad specifications had not been given in detail.
choices.zh: 广告规格没有详细给出。

choices.text: The woman's company made last-minute changes.
choices.zh: 这位女士的公司在最后时刻做了变更。

choices.text: Organising the promotion was really time-consuming.
choices.zh: 组织这次促销活动确实很耗时。

items.stem: What does the woman propose as a solution to the problem?

choices.text: Run another four-week campaign.
choices.zh: 再开展一次为期四周的促销活动。

choices.text: Give her a 10 percent discount.
choices.zh: 给她打九折。

choices.text: Extend the campaign to next year.
choices.zh: 把促销活动延续到明年。

choices.text: Cut the fee by half for this year.
choices.zh: 把今年的费用减半。

items.stem: What does the man suggest they do at the end of the conversation?

choices.text: Calm down and make peace.
choices.zh: 冷静下来和解。

choices.text: Improve their promotion plans.
choices.zh: 改进他们的促销计划。

choices.text: Stop negotiating for the time being.
choices.zh: 暂时停止协商。

choices.text: Reflect on their respective mistakes.
choices.zh: 反思各自的错误。

items.stem: What does the passage say about most of the mice used for experiments?

choices.text: They are labeled pet animals by the researchers.
choices.zh: 研究人员将它们标记为宠物动物。

choices.text: They look spotlessly clean throughout their lives.
choices.zh: 它们终其一生看起来都一尘不染。

choices.text: They are looked after by animal-care organizations.
choices.zh: 它们由动物保护组织照料。

choices.text: They sacrifice their lives for the benefit of humans.
choices.zh: 它们为人类的利益牺牲了生命。

items.stem: Why did the so-called bad mice have to be captured and destroyed?

choices.text: They may behave abnormally.
choices.zh: 它们可能会表现异常。

choices.text: They may breed out of control.
choices.zh: 它们可能会失控繁殖。

choices.text: They may affect the results of experiments.
choices.zh: 它们可能会影响实验结果。

choices.text: They may cause damage to the environment.
choices.zh: 它们可能会对环境造成破坏。

items.stem: When are mice killed without prior approval?

choices.text: When they are no longer useful.
choices.zh: 当它们不再有用时。

choices.text: when they become ill.
choices.zh: 当它们生病时。

choices.text: When they become escapees.
choices.zh: 当它们成为逃跑者时。

choices.text: when they get too old.
choices.zh: 当它们变得太老时。

items.stem: Why does the speaker say what the Herzogs did at home is ironical?

choices.text: While holding a burial ceremony for a pet mouse, they were killing pest mice.
choices.zh: 在为一只宠物鼠举行葬礼的同时,他们正在杀害害鼠。

choices.text: While advocating freedom for animals, they kept their pet mouse in a cage.
choices.zh: 在倡导动物自由的同时,他们把宠物鼠关在笼子里。

choices.text: While calling for animal rights, they allowed their kids to keep pet animals.
choices.zh: 在呼吁动物权利的同时,他们允许孩子饲养宠物动物。

choices.text: While launching animal protection campaigns, they were trapping kitchen mice.
choices.zh: 在发起动物保护运动的同时,他们正在捕捉厨房里的老鼠。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about the natives of New York?

choices.text: They contribute most to it.
choices.zh: 他们对纽约贡献最大。

choices.text: They are crazy about it.
choices.zh: 他们对纽约极为狂热。

choices.text: They often find fault with it.
choices.zh: 他们常常挑剔纽约。

choices.text: They take it for granted.
choices.zh: 他们认为纽约理所当然。

items.stem: What does the speaker say commuters give to New York?

choices.text: Tidal restlessness.
choices.zh: 潮汐般的躁动不安。

choices.text: Heat and light.
choices.zh: 热量和光亮。

choices.text: Economic prosperity.
choices.zh: 经济繁荣。

choices.text: Historical continuity.
choices.zh: 历史延续性。

items.stem: What do we learn about the settlers of New York?

choices.text: They lack knowledge of the culture of the city.
choices.zh: 他们缺乏对这座城市文化的了解。

choices.text: They are adventurers from all over the world.
choices.zh: 他们是来自世界各地的冒险者。

choices.text: They have difficulty surviving.
choices.zh: 他们难以生存。

choices.text: They find the city alien to them.
choices.zh: 他们觉得这座城市与自己格格不入。

items.stem: According to Professor Dreiser, which of the following discoveries was made during the first era in the history of nutrition?

choices.text: Protein was recognized as an essential component of diet.
choices.zh: 蛋白质被认定为饮食的基本组成部分。

choices.text: Vitamins were synthesized from foods.
choices.zh: 维生素是从食物中合成的。

choices.text: Effective measures of weight loss were determined.
choices.zh: 确定了有效的减重措施。

choices.text: Certain foods were found to be harmful to good health.
choices.zh: 某些食物被发现对健康有害。

items.stem: What is the purpose of teaching concepts of nutrition in medical schools?

choices.text: In order to urge medical doctors to participate in research studies on nutrition.
choices.zh: 为了敦促医生参与营养学研究。

choices.text: In order to encourage medical doctors to apply concepts of nutrition in the treatment of disease.
choices.zh: 为了鼓励医生在疾病治疗中应用营养学概念。

choices.text: In order to persuade doctors to conduct experimental vitamin therapies on their patients.
choices.zh: 为了说服医生对患者实施实验性维生素疗法。

choices.text: In order to support the creation of artificial vitamins.
choices.zh: 为了支持人工维生素的研制。

items.stem: Why did vitamin therapy become less popular in the 1950s?

choices.text: The public lost interest in vitamins.
choices.zh: 公众对维生素失去了兴趣。

choices.text: Medical schools stopped teaching nutritional concepts.
choices.zh: 医学院停止讲授营养学概念。

choices.text: Nutritional research was of poor quality.
choices.zh: 营养学研究质量低劣。

choices.text: Claims for the effectiveness of vitamin therapy were exaggerated.
choices.zh: 维生素疗法有效性的宣称被夸大了。

items.stem: What does the talk mainly discuss?

choices.text: How babies differentiate between the sound of the human voice and other sounds.
choices.zh: 婴儿如何区分人类声音和其他声音。

choices.text: The differences between a baby's and an adult's ability to comprehend language.
choices.zh: 婴儿和成人理解语言能力的差异。

choices.text: How babies perceive and respond to the human voice in their early stages of language development.
choices.zh: 婴儿在语言发展早期阶段如何感知和回应人类声音。

choices.text: The response of a baby to sounds other than the human voice.
choices.zh: 婴儿对人类声音以外的声音的反应。

items.stem: Why does the speaker mention the ringing of a bell?

choices.text: To contrast the reactions of babies to human and nonhuman sounds.
choices.zh: 为了对比婴儿对人类声音和非人类声音的反应。

choices.text: To give examples of sounds that will cause a baby to cry.
choices.zh: 为了举例说明会导致婴儿哭泣的声音。

choices.text: To explain how babies distinguish between different nonhuman sounds.
choices.zh: 为了解释婴儿如何区分不同的非人类声音。

choices.text: To give examples of typical toys that babies do not like.
choices.zh: 为了举例说明婴儿不喜欢的典型玩具。

items.stem: What can we learn from the findings of babies and their mothers in six diverse cultures?

choices.text: Babies who are exposed to more than one language can acquire languages earlier than those to a single language.
choices.zh: 接触多种语言的婴儿比接触单一语言的婴儿能更早习得语言。

choices.text: Mothers from different cultures speak to their babies in a similar way.
choices.zh: 来自不同文化的母亲以相似的方式对婴儿说话。

choices.text: Babies ignore facial expressions in comprehending their parents' language.
choices.zh: 婴儿在理解父母语言时忽略面部表情。

choices.text: The mothers observed by the researchers were consciously teaching their babies to speak.
choices.zh: 研究人员观察到的母亲在有意识地教婴儿说话。

items.stem: According to the talk, why do babies listen to songs and stories, even though they cannot understand them?

choices.text: They understand the rhythm.
choices.zh: 他们理解节奏。

choices.text: They enjoy the sounds of them.
choices.zh: 他们喜欢这些声音。

choices.text: They can remember them easily.
choices.zh: 他们能轻易记住这些内容。

choices.text: They focus on their parents' words.
choices.zh: 他们专注于父母的话语。

items.stem: According to the talk, which country played a leading role in the invention and promotion of cinema?

choices.text: Britain.
choices.zh: 英国。

choices.text: Germany.
choices.zh: 德国。

choices.text: France.
choices.zh: 法国。

choices.text: Japan.
choices.zh: 日本。

items.stem: According to the talk, what can we learn about the film market back then?

choices.text: The United States had a leading position on the world market by the start of World War I.
choices.zh: 到第一次世界大战开始时,美国在世界市场上已处于领先地位。

choices.text: The centre of film-making moved eastwards from Hollywood to New York.
choices.zh: 电影制作中心从好莱坞向东转移到了纽约。

choices.text: Many film industries could compete with that of Hollywood.
choices.zh: 许多电影产业都能与好莱坞的电影产业竞争。

choices.text: The film markets of Russia and Japan were the only promising ones.
choices.zh: 俄罗斯和日本的电影市场是仅有的有前景的市场。

items.stem: What is the speaker's attitude towards the film industry?

choices.text: Indifferent.
choices.zh: 漠不关心。

choices.text: Biased.
choices.zh: 有偏见。

choices.text: Negative.
choices.zh: 消极。

choices.text: Neutral.
choices.zh: 中立。
